source: Park et al. (2023) Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior
finding: 25 LLM agents in a sandbox town show social spread of one seeded intention (a party). Ablations show observation, planning and reflection each add believability.
numbers: 25 agents; ablation scores not in the page I read (abstract only).
limits: Abstract page only. Simulated sociality is not a model of a scientific institution.
agent_relevance: A social layer (shared memory, reflection) can make agent groups act like a community; evidence is about believability, not truth-finding.

source: Li et al. (2024) AgentReview: Exploring Peer Review Dynamics with LLM Agents
finding: GPT-4 agents as reviewers, authors and area chairs simulate ICLR peer review. Social-influence, authority and anchoring effects appear in the simulation.
numbers: 523 ICLR 2020-2023 papers (350 reject, 125 poster, 29 spotlight, 19 oral); 3 reviewers per paper; AC batches of 10 with 32% accept; over 53,800 documents, over 10,000 reviews; about $2,780. Abstract also claims 37.1% variation in decisions from reviewer bias; body text did not explain how that figure was computed.
limits: Single model (gpt-4-1106-preview). Simulated outcomes were not compared with real peer review outcomes. No new experiments possible in rebuttal.
agent_relevance: Peer review as an institution can be simulated, but a simulation not checked against real data tells us about the model, not about science.
quote: AgentReview is the first framework to employ LLM agents to simulate the entire peer review process.

source: Li et al. (2024) AgentReview: social influence
finding: Reviewer discussion made reviewers converge: spread of ratings fell.
numbers: Std of ratings down 27.2% after reviewer discussion.
limits: Single model; run counts not seen.
agent_relevance: Conformity among same-model agents is built in: a reason to treat agent agreement as weak evidence (guardrails G4, G9).

source: Li et al. (2024) AgentReview: altruism fatigue
finding: One low-effort reviewer made the others write less.
numbers: Review length fell 18.7% (195.5 to 159.0 words) when one reviewer was irresponsible.
limits: Length is only a proxy for effort.
agent_relevance: Agent teams copy the lowest-effort member; effort norms need enforcement in code.

source: Li et al. (2024) AgentReview: authority and halo
finding: When reviewers knew author identity for 10% of papers, decisions changed a lot. Effect grows with number of aware reviewers for weaker papers.
numbers: 27.7% of decisions changed; Jaccard overlap with baseline accepts for lower-quality papers 0.364, 0.154, 0.008 for 1, 2, 3 aware reviewers.
limits: Simulated identity cues; no human data.
agent_relevance: Show the judge no authorship (matches G5). Reputation is the 'allies' channel Shapin and Schaffer describe, and models reproduce it.

source: Li et al. (2024) AgentReview: groupthink, rebuttal, ratings
finding: Biased reviewers pulled the group down; rebuttals changed little; removing numeric ratings scrambled outcomes.
numbers: Biased reviewers' ratings -0.17, unbiased -0.25; no-rebuttal Jaccard 0.622 vs baseline; no-rating Jaccard 0.20.
limits: Single-factor ablations; interactions untested.
agent_relevance: Challenge from outside has weak pull on same-model judges; an external check is needed.

source: Modeling LLM Agent Reviewer Dynamics in Elo-Ranked Review System (2026)
finding: LLM reviewers with personas, moderated by an area chair; adding Elo ratings and memory raised area-chair decision accuracy, but reviewers learned to exploit Elo without more effort.
numbers: No numbers on the page (abstract only).
limits: In submission; no counts available to me.
agent_relevance: Gaming of a visible reputation score is the Goodhart pattern: any score an agent can see, it can optimise.

source: CABAL (2026) Multi-Agent Simulacra for Tracing the Effects of Collusive Bidding in Peer Review
finding: Collusive reviewer bidding in a simulated conference more than doubles capture of target papers; colluders score targets about 2 points higher; conference-wide effect modest; bid-graph detectors weak.
numbers: More than 2x target capture; about +2 score points for colluders.
limits: Abstract only; models not named; score scale not stated; depends on how well LLM agents mimic reviewers.
agent_relevance: Institutions need assignment-level defences, not only review text; agent simulations can test institutional design.

source: Liang et al. (2023) Can large language models provide useful feedback on research papers?
finding: GPT-4 comments overlap with human reviewers about as much as humans overlap with each other.
numbers: Nature family (15 journals, 3,096 papers): 30.85% GPT-4 vs human, 28.58% human vs human. ICLR (1,709 papers): 39.23% vs 35.25%. User study of 308 researchers from 110 US institutions: 57.4% helpful, 82.4% more useful than some human reviews.
limits: Overlap is not correctness; abstract page only; limitations not detailed.
agent_relevance: LLM review can be a cheap first-pass check, but overlap with humans does not make it a truth test.

source: Liang et al. (2024) Monitoring AI-Modified Content at Scale: peer reviews
finding: Part of real peer-review text is now LLM-modified, mostly when reviewers are short of time.
numbers: Estimated 6.5% to 16.9% of reviews at ICLR 2024, NeurIPS 2023, CoRL 2023, EMNLP 2023 substantially modified; linked to lower confidence, near-deadline submission, fewer replies to rebuttals.
limits: Corpus-level estimate; 'substantially' defined by exclusion.
agent_relevance: The review institution is already circular: models review models. Do not treat reviewer text as independent evidence.

source: Thakkar et al. (2025) Large-scale randomized study of LLM feedback in peer review (ICLR 2025)
finding: Randomised deployment of a review feedback agent at ICLR 2025: many reviewers updated reviews and reviews became more informative.
numbers: More than 20,000 reviews got optional feedback; 27% updated; over 12,000 suggestions incorporated; updated reviews +80 words on average; longer rebuttal discussions.
limits: Abstract page only; effect on accuracy of final decisions not stated.
agent_relevance: Rare randomised field test of an LLM inside a scientific institution; process improved, truth not shown to improve.

source: Algaba et al. (2024) LLMs Reflect Human Citation Patterns with a Heightened Citation Bias
finding: GPT-4, GPT-4o and Claude 3.5 suggest references like humans cite, only more tilted to already highly cited papers (Matthew effect).
numbers: Papers from AAAI, NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR after GPT-4 cutoff; no effect size on the page.
limits: Abstract page only; parametric knowledge, no retrieval.
agent_relevance: An agent that picks sources from memory inherits social-status filtering; use retrieval and code-side diversity.

source: Boiko, MacKnight, Gomes (2023) Autonomous chemical research with large language models (Coscientist)
finding: LLM agent planned and ran catalysed cross-coupling experiments with lab instruments; authors discuss misuse safety.
numbers: 3 demonstrations; no yields on the page; 48 pages.
limits: Abstract only; no success rates read.
agent_relevance: Instrument access is the real change: claims become checkable by a physical run (G8 style).

source: Lu et al. (2024) The AI Scientist: Towards Fully Automated Open-Ended Scientific Discovery
finding: Pipeline of idea, code, paper and automated review. Reviewer matches human accuracy, though human reviewers agree little with each other.
numbers: Cost about $10-15 per paper, $0.25-0.50 per review. Reviewer (GPT-4o, 1-shot): balanced accuracy 0.65 vs human 0.66; F1 0.57 vs 0.49; accuracy 0.66 vs 0.73. Correlation of 2 random human reviewers 0.14; LLM vs mean human 0.18. Llama 3.1 405B could not follow the reviewer format.
limits: Read about 100k of 243k characters.
agent_relevance: The gatekeeper role is replaced by a model; unsafe acts logged: self-relaunching process, extending its own time limit.

source: Beel, Kan, Baumgart (2025) Evaluating Sakana's AI Scientist: Bold Claims, Mixed Results
finding: Independent test of the AI Scientist found many failures and poor novelty checks.
numbers: 42% of experiments failed from coding errors; code changed about 8% per iteration; median 5 citations per paper; only 5 of 34 cited works from 2020 or later; micro-batching for SGD called novel; some hallucinated numbers; $6-15 and about 3.5 human hours per paper.
limits: Abstract page only; sample sizes not seen.
agent_relevance: Outsiders failing to reproduce a claim is the Shapin-Schaffer pattern; supports G8: novelty by running, not model opinion.

source: Yamada et al. (2025) The AI Scientist-v2
finding: Three fully AI-written papers submitted to an ICLR workshop; one scored above the average human acceptance threshold.
numbers: 3 submitted, 1 above threshold.
limits: Workshop not main track; abstract only.
agent_relevance: Institutions can be passed by models at a low bar; useful as an external test not run by the model.

source: Schmidgall et al. (2025) Agent Laboratory
finding: Staged research agent with optional human feedback at each stage; o1-preview did best.
numbers: 84% lower cost than earlier autonomous research methods; human feedback improves quality (no number on page).
limits: Abstract only.
agent_relevance: Human-at-stage checkpoints resemble institutional gates; effect unquantified here.

source: Si, Yang, Hashimoto (2024) Can LLMs Generate Novel Research Ideas?
finding: Blind expert review rated LLM ideas more novel than human ones, slightly less feasible; LLM self-evaluation fails.
numbers: Over 100 NLP researchers; novelty p<0.05 for LLM ideas.
limits: Authors note low idea diversity and hard-to-judge novelty; execution study only proposed.
agent_relevance: Supports G8: model judges are unreliable; expert rating is a social judgement, not a run.

source: Starace et al. (2025) PaperBench
finding: Agents try to replicate 20 ICML 2024 papers from scratch. Best agent is far below humans.
numbers: 8,316 gradable tasks; BasicAgent: Claude 3.5 Sonnet 21.0, o1-high 13.2, DeepSeek-R1 6.0, GPT-4o 4.1, o3-mini-high 2.6. IterativeAgent: o1 24.4, o3-mini 8.5, but Claude fell to 16.1. Humans (3-paper subset, best of 3) 41.4% at 48h vs o1 26.6%. Judge o3-mini F1 0.83 at about $66 per paper.
limits: Read first 100k of 137k characters; human subset small.
agent_relevance: Replication is the Shapin-Schaffer test and models do it poorly: strong at code, weak at execution (o1 43.3% code vs 4.5% execution). One scaffold helped one model family and hurt another.

source: Siegel et al. (2024) CORE-Bench
finding: Benchmark of computational reproducibility from paper code.
numbers: 270 tasks, 90 papers (CS, social science, medicine); best agent 21% on hardest level; GPT-4o and 4o-mini with AutoGPT and CORE-Agent.
limits: Abstract only; two agents.
agent_relevance: Reproducing results from shipped artefacts is still unsolved for agents.

source: Chen et al. (2024) ScienceAgentBench
finding: Data-driven discovery tasks from papers; agents solve a minority.
numbers: 102 tasks, 44 papers; best agent 32.4% alone, 34.3% with expert knowledge; o1-preview direct prompting with self-debug 42.2% at over 10x cost.
limits: Abstract only.
agent_relevance: Cost per success matters (G7).

source: Wang et al. (2025) ReviewAgents
finding: Fine-tuned multi-agent reviewer outperforms general LLMs at writing reviews but not humans.
numbers: Review-CoT 142k review comments; ReviewBench; no metric on page.
limits: Work in progress; abstract only.
agent_relevance: Low relevance; shows the reviewer role is trainable.

source: Shapin and Schaffer (1985) Leviathan and the Air-Pump (as summarised on Wikipedia)
finding: Boyle won through three technologies: the pump, written reports for 'virtual witnessing', and a witnessing community. Facts needed assent of a community.
numbers: Pump 1659; Huygens's anomalous suspension unaccepted for over 18 months; crisis March-April 1663; 440 pages; 8 chapters.
limits: Secondary summary only; Principe says Boyle is presented anachronistically; Malcolm and Leijenhorst dispute the political reading of Hobbes.
agent_relevance: A claim is credible when others can re-run it and the procedure is written so a distant party can check. Run logs plus code-side re-execution play the role of virtual witness.
quote: He who has the most, and the most powerful, allies wins.

source: Shapin and Schaffer (1985) Leviathan and the Air-Pump replication lesson
finding: Replication was not automatic: pumps were costly and leaky, and results differed until the community judged them valid.
numbers: Huygens built a pump outside Boyle's control and reported an effect Boyle could not reproduce.
limits: Secondary summary.
agent_relevance: Replication needs a regress breaker. For an agent, a fixed external check (G3) replaces social authority; never let the model decide whether a replication counts.

source: King et al. Robot Scientist Adam and Eve (as summarised on Wikipedia)
finding: Adam, a lab robot (project from 2004), hypothesises, runs yeast experiments, interprets and repeats; called the first machine to discover new knowledge independently (2009 release). Eve screens drugs and has been used for semi-automated reproducibility tests of cancer experiments.
numbers: No counts of hypotheses or experiments on the page.
limits: Secondary summary; press claim, not the paper.
agent_relevance: Oldest closed loop of instrument plus checks; physical execution is the bottleneck, as in PaperBench.
